Study Layout

Experience

Lesson Goal

Use simple English when you travel to another country by plane, train, bus, or taxi. Ask for help, check tickets, find the right place, and make a safe backup plan.

Introduction

When you travel in another country, transport English does not need to be perfect. It needs to be clear.

You often need the same information again and again: where to go, what time to leave, how much to pay, and what to do if something changes.

This lesson follows Maya. She is going from her hotel to another country for a short trip.

She uses a taxi, a plane, a train, and a bus. The goal is not to learn travel words for fun.

The goal is to use English that helps you move safely and calmly.

Warm-Up Questions

  • Have you ever taken transport in another country?
  • What feels difficult at an airport, station, or bus stop?
  • What information do you need before you get on transport?
  • Who can you ask for help when you are not sure?

Final Reflection

Good transport English is simple and practical. Check the destination.

Check the ticket. Find the gate, platform, or stop.

Ask about delays. Make a backup plan.

You can use short questions many times: "Where is ...? ", "Which platform?

", "Does this go to ...? ", "How much is it?

", "How long is the delay? ", and "Can you help me?

"

Final Speaking Task

Useful Speaking Patterns

  • Excuse me. Where is ...?
  • Which platform for ...?
  • Which gate for ...?
  • Does this train go to ...?
  • Does this bus stop near ...?
  • Can I pay by card?
  • How long is the delay?
  • Is there another train or bus?
  • Can you tell me when we get to ...?

Practice Questions

  • Which transport situation feels most stressful for you?
  • What phrase from this lesson do you want to remember?
  • When should you show your phone instead of trying to explain?
  • Why is it useful to repeat important information?
  • What is your backup plan if you miss a train, bus, or flight?
